newsitem.title: GERMANY: Workers occupy bankrupt E.German aluminium plant.
newsitem.headline: Workers occupy bankrupt E.German aluminium plant.

text.p: Some 200 workers at bankrupt eastern German aluminium processor Rackwitz occupied their plant on Friday in a bid to stop the feared sale of machinery and equipment, the plant's works council said.
Although the plant was idle because there were no raw materials, workers would keep occupy it over the Christmas and New Year holiday period, it said.
They would carry out maintenance work to keep the plant ready for a restart in case money was found to save it.
Local courts said on Tuesday the company had filed for bankruptcy proceedings because it could no longer meet its financial obligations.

The plant, which was sold by privatisation agency Treuhand to the West German Gottschol group in 1994, received large sums in public investment aid, but posted losses during an aluminium demand lull and due to start-up problems with new machinery.
It produced 1,800 tonnes a month of processed metal last year, mostly sections for the building industry and foil.
The offical receiver and the state of Saxony aim to maintain production at Rackwitz with its 350 jobs and at another site in Merseburg, which employs another 100.

Three more re-rollers in Berlin and west Germany owned by the private Gottschol group started bankruptcy proceedings on Wednesday. An analyst attributed this to overcapacity in aluminium products for the flagging building sector.
